In a stunning move that has left fans and pundits alike scratching their heads, Spanish association football player Víctor Mollejo has announced that he is leaving the pitch behind to pursue a new passion: college basketball. The 22-year-old winger, who has played for top-tier clubs in Spain, has enrolled at the University of Delaware and will suit up for the Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball team. "I've always had a love for basketball, and I figured, why not take on a new challenge?" Mollejo said in an exclusive interview with our publication. "I'm excited to bring my competitive spirit and work ethic to the court and help the Blue Hens make a run in the NCAA tournament." Mollejo, who stands at 5'9", may not be the tallest player on the court, but his speed, agility, and endurance – honed from years of playing football at the highest level – could prove to be a game-changer for the Blue Hens. "Víctor is an incredible athlete, and we're thrilled to have him on board," said Delaware head coach Martin Ingelsby. "He's already shown a natural aptitude for the game, and we're confident that he'll be a valuable asset to our team." According to sources close to the program, Mollejo has been working out with the team for several weeks, impressing coaches and teammates alike with his quick learning curve and tenacious defense. "I was skeptical at first, but Víctor has been a sponge," said junior guard Ryan Allen. "He's picked up our system fast, and his energy is infectious. We're all excited to see what he can do on the court." Mollejo's decision to trade in his cleats for sneakers has sent shockwaves through the football community, with many of his former teammates and coaches expressing surprise and admiration for his bold move. "Víctor is a true competitor, and I have no doubt he'll excel in whatever he sets his mind to," said former teammate and Spanish football star, Sergio Ramos. "I'll be rooting for him from afar, and I'm excited to see how he'll adapt to the college basketball scene." As Mollejo prepares to take the court for the Blue Hens, fans are eagerly anticipating his debut.

"cards": one card for each answer the document itself gives to the question. Usually that is one card. - "entity": who or what this answer is about, as specifically as the document identifies it: the full name, plus the details the document gives that tell it apart from others with the same name (what kind of thing it is, profession or role, nationality or place, years, creator, other names), even where the question does not ask about them. - "sense": which event, edition, version, condition, place or measure the answer refers to, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "answer": the answer, copied from the document as it is written there, and short: a full name, a date, a number with its unit, or a short phrase. For a yes-or-no question, "yes" or "no".
- "as_of": the date at which this was true, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "claim_kind": "factual", or "opinion" for a judgment, a recommendation or a contested finding.
- "attributed_to": who or what the document says this comes from, such as a census, a study or a named person, if it says; otherwise "not stated".
- "evidence": the sentence of the document that gives the answer, copied word for word. Two sentences if one is not enough.
- "claim": one sentence that states the answer on its own and names the entity.
